  1.  Establish a process to accommodate outdoor dining in the following ways
  and allow these conditions to remain in place until November 30, 2020 or
  when occupancy is permitted at 100%

  2. Allow restaurants to request an increase in the allowable public and
  private space available for outdoor dining: relax outdoor dining
  regulations, development standards and conditions of approval, and to
  establish regulations which allow outdoor consumption of alcohol at
  restaurants where indoor consumption of alcohol was already allowed;

  3. Waive fees associated to these requests

  4. Allow for parking requirements to be reduced for increased outdoor
  dining space with a property owner's permission; and

  5. Grant staff the authority to make administrative adjustments as needed
  to previously approved Use Permits and other entitlement mechanisms.

11  Community Development  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the Community
  Block Grant Business  Development Block Grant Business Assistance Grant. He stated that the City
  Assistance Grant  Council recently approved a Business Assistance Grant program that would
  offer one-time $2,500 grants to eligible businesses to help them re-open,
  create Jobs, retain jobs, and offer quality services to the residents of La Verne
  The program is funded through a grant from the U.S. Department of Housing
  and Urban Development. Due to limited response, the deadline has been
  extended to June 5, 2020. Additionally, the Economic Development
  Committee and staff are recommending that the City Council approve further
  tiers that would make funds available to more businesses in the event there
  are unused funds.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment and waited a few minutes for staff to
  check for any public comments received by email.

  There was none.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Crosby, and unanimously carried to
  extend the deadline for the Business Assistance Grant applications to Friday
  June 5, 2020 and establish additional tiers to allow for more applications to
  be considered until the allocated funding is utilized.

City of La Verne City Council
Public Comments
June 1, 2020

Good evening Mayor Hepburn, Mayor Pro Tern Carder, Council Member Davis, Council
Member Lau, and Council Member Lau

In the months and weeks of the runup to the City election this past March, I often saw the
term "forensic audit" used in local social media posts. This was generally from people who
were associated with the very politically active organization LVC3. This organization denies
being an unregistered Political Action Committee even though Federal Election Law defines a
PAC as any organization that receives or spends $1,000 or more to influence an election. They
also deny they endorse any political candidate. They may not "officially" endorse any
candidate but by their actions they ta citly endorsed candidates. There is nothing wrong with
being politically active as an individual or within an organization but when you are, just own
it. I dismissed the language as political rhetoric, or political sou nd bytes from persons who
were not familiar with an actual forensic audit or the need of such investigation of financial
data; the processes involved, and the actual purpose of such an audit. Also, in those social
media posts the t erm forensic audit was also generally followed or preceded by a
condemnation of funds spent on lawsuits the City was involved. Knowing what a forensic
audit involved and that lawsuit strategy was not something that necessitated such audit I
merely passed this off as more uninformed political rhetoric.

When the agenda item was discussed, I was pleased that Council Member Lau articulated
what the uses of forensic audit were and what necessitates such an audit. She very thoroughly
explained the purposes, intents, and limitations of such audit. Forensic audits are very specific
and are used in instances where theft and/or embezzlement using complex and sophisticated
processes to divert money from the organization to personal uses are suspected. A forensic
audit is an investigative tool to expose such criminal behavior. However, this seemed to be
ignored by Mayor Hepburn and also his call in supporter Mr. Rick Bowen as they continued to
press for such audit; even though it was explained that it would be a very expensive process
that was not applicable to the circumstances stated; and the further negative effect upon the
 current already stressed City budget due to the effects of the covid 19 lockdown. The City's
finances are already audited by a professional accounting firm on a regularly scheduled basis,
and the accuracy and professionalism of our staff results in outstanding audit resu lts as
evidenced in the recent bond process to address CALPERS needs. Looking for audit resu lts to
address lawsuit strategies is an expensive exercise in futility. The strategies for dealing with
lawsuits is the responsibility of the City Council as a whole, not with the Finance Department.

It was t hen apparent that the agenda item was merely an attempt at keeping a political
promise to supporters in the last election and not for the actual good of the community at
large.

I sincerely hope that these attempts cease immediately. There is much work ahead of our City
to come out of the pandemic lockdown and promote local business growth and sustain a good
quality of life for our citilens without these unnecessary distractions.

Terry Prentice
2986 Wenwood St
La Verne, CA

Linda Lockhart Wilkinson , 32 year La Verne resident and business owner.

I am a Plaintiff in a pending lawsuit against the City of La Verne and former Mayor
Kendrick. As the Council may be aware, I filed my lawsuit because City Manager Russi
offered my tenant, Chase's Restaurant, approximately $80,000 in taxpayer money to
move out of my property almost 2 years before their lease was up, and move to their new
location on Bonita. Former Mayor Kendrick voted when he should have been recused
because his real estate business was across the street from the Bonita location. The City
should not have interfered with my contract and inserted itself between a landlord and
tenant. I was harmed by the City's actions because when Chase's abandoned my
property, my property lost its Health Department permit to operate a restaurant, and lost
some grandfathered rights for my kitchen operation. I was shocked that the City did this,
and I have tried my best to rebuild my business, at great expense.

I love La Verne and only want to resolve this matter on reasonable terms and move
forward . I raised my sons in La Verne and was proud to watch them grow up here. I
bought a family section of La Verne Cemetery and buried my parents here. I've invested
financially into a city that I love and support. I want to get my property up and running
again . I am prepared to settle the case on reasonable terms. I am concerned that the full
Council is not being kept informed about the case. I request that the Council agendize the
matter for the next closed session, consider my written settlement offer, and agree to
attend a mediation.

Thank you for your anticipated cooperation and response.
